claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2 text adds the round-1 condition ("when the code that calls or implements an interface needs different parts of it, split it"). Pinned docs frame ISP per dependent: "Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." (options.md:12). The unconditional ranking is gone; the split is now conditional and consistent with section 6.

"A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." (interfaces.md:86). Lesson now says "apart from any the interface gives a body of its own", matching the exception. CS0535 fix: "Provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface, or declare the type as abstract" (interface-implementation-errors.md:140).

Unchanged from round 1. Execution (SDK 10, net10.0): implementer keeping GetDeliveryReport(int) after the interface changed to GetDeliveryReport(int, bool) gave "error CS0535: 'Sms' does not implement interface member 'IChannel.GetDeliveryReport(int, bool)'". Doc: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35).
git show stage-0:.../INotifier.cs lines 5-8: `public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }` - one member. Code block lines=5-8 matches character-for-character.

git show stage-0: line 5 `public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier`; line 7 private `List<string> sent`; line 9 `IReadOnlyList<string> Sent => sent`; lines 11-16 Send calls Format, sent.Add, Console.WriteLine; line 18 `protected abstract string Format(...)`; lines 21-31 EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier override only Format. Code block lines=21-31 matches.

`git -C examples/don-hang grep -n -i deliver stage-0 -- samples` returns no lines. No INotificationChannel or GetDeliveryReport at stage-0. `git grep -i confirm stage-0` and `stage-1` also return nothing, so the confirmation code is not in the samples either.

"C# doesn't have the concept of checked exceptions. Any method might (in theory) throw any exception." (tips-for-java-developers.md:16) - nothing in the interface signature tells a caller that one implementation throws. The LSP link restates the prerequisite lesson.
Design judgement restating outline misconception 2, not a version-dependent fact. Consistent with the pinned per-dependent framing of ISP (options.md:12), which says nothing about member count.

Doc: implicit reference conversion when "assigning a reference type instance to a variable of an interface the type implements" (conversions.md:46). Execution (SDK 10, stage-0 INotifier.cs + NotifierBase.cs copied verbatim): `INotifier[] all = { new EmailNotifier(), new SmsNotifier() }; foreach (INotifier n in all) n.Send(7, "placed");` builds and prints "email about order 7: placed" / "sms about order 7: placed".

Only a type that implements the interface converts to it (conversions.md:46), and implementing requires every member without a default body (interfaces.md:86). Execution (SDK 10): passing `new SmsOnly()` (has SendSms only) to `Use(IChannel c)` with IChannel{SendEmail; SendSms} gives "error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'SmsOnly' to 'IChannel'".

issues.text: q6 fill: answer set accepts only "INotifier" (case-insensitive, trimmed). The namespace-qualified name "DonHang.Samples.Oop.INotifier", which is also correct, and a backticked "`INotifier`" are both rejected.

The prose tells me to look for a left half (proposal) and a right half (samples). But the diagram is one left-to-right flow, so SmsNotifier-under-proposal, confirmation code, EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier all sit in the first column, INotificationChannel and NotifierBase in the next, INotifier last. The two halves appear one above the other and mixed by column, not side by side. I had to work out which nodes belong to which half from the labels.
issues.quote: The left half of the diagram is the proposal; the right half is what the samples have today.
issues.fix: Name the parts without position, e.g. "The first two arrows (into INotificationChannel) are the proposal; the last three (NotifierBase, EmailNotifier, SmsNotifier, INotifier) are what the samples have today."

issues.text: The correction is now clear, but the belief itself still says 'every class implementing it ... uses every method', which read literally is the case misconception 2 calls fine ('every implementer needs all three'). The correction then answers a different belief ('each method is used by some class somewhere'). q2's statement already has the clearer wording.
issues.quote: A big interface is fine as long as every class implementing it eventually uses every method somewhere.
issues.fix: Reword the belief to match q2 and the correction: "A big interface is fine as long as each of its methods is used by some class somewhere." Update q2's `misconception` field to the same text.

issues.text: I read this twice: 'apart from any the interface gives a body of its own' is hard to parse ('gives ... of its own' vs 'gives a body to'), and it raises the new idea that interface methods can have bodies. The trailing 'none of these four has one' does tell me I can ignore it.
issues.quote: apart from any the interface gives a body of its own — and none of these four has one
issues.fix: Replace with "apart from any the interface already gives a body to — and none of these four has one".

issues.text: q1 correct explanation is missing its verb: 'C# requires every interface method that the interface does not give a body of its own' — requires it to do what? I have to guess 'to be provided by the class'.
issues.quote: C# requires every interface method that the interface does not give a body of its own, so `SmsNotifier` would need filler
issues.fix: Rewrite as "C# requires a class to provide every interface method the interface does not already give a body to, so `SmsNotifier` would need filler ..." and mirror in vi.
